evidence_gaps_add: Ahlmann-Eltze et al. 2025 (Nature Methods), the main independent comparison of foundation and deep models against additive, mean and linear baselines, reports its per-method results only in figures; its Source Data are per-perturbation rows. Not extracted.
Control-aware metrics (Systema, Nature Biotechnology 2025) are reported only in figures; no printed per-method values were found.
The one extracted comparison (Csendes et al. 2025) has one split per dataset, no spread, author-built baselines and author-reproduced foundation models.
PerturBench combination-prediction results are in the store as task records and need a protocol before they can be judged for this use case.
use_case_changes.setting_note: No setting change is proposed. The setting is anchored to GEARS Table 6 and is pinned by the existing judgements; widening it to name Csendes et al. would withhold them until re-review.

summary_proposal.source_locator: perturbation-response-20261009-source-csendes2025-supp: Supplementary Table 2 column 'Pearson Delta' for models 'mean', 'scGPT', 'scFoundation' and 'RF_go'
summary_proposal.text: In an independent benchmark on four Perturb-seq datasets (Csendes et al. 2025), a control that predicts the mean training response for every unseen perturbation scored a higher Pearson correlation of expression change than both foundation models on all four: 0.71, 0.56, 0.37 and 0.63 for Adamson, Norman, Replogle K562 and Replogle RPE1, against 0.64, 0.55, 0.33 and 0.60 for scGPT and 0.55, 0.46, 0.27 and 0.47 for scFoundation. A random forest on Gene Ontology features of the perturbed gene scored 0.74, 0.59, 0.48 and 0.65. The baselines were built by the authors, who also re-ran the foundation models; there is one split per dataset and no spread. The authors note that these datasets have little perturbation-specific variance, so they separate models poorly. Expression scores do not show which experiments will succeed.

number_trace.little perturbation-specific variance: Results 'Limited perturbation diversity biases benchmarking outcomes'; limitation on each protocol

summary_proposal.caveat_note: Values are rounded to two decimals in the text; Norman Train Mean (0.557266) and scGPT (0.553838) differ by 0.003.

gaps: Csendes et al. Supplementary Table 3 (Norman subgroups): the metric column is unlabelled; the Supplementary Figure 1 legend suggests Pearson delta, but that was not taken as a label. Not extracted.
No source measures experimental hit rate or prioritisation success.
GEARS itself is not among the Csendes et al. configurations (scFoundation runs inside GEARS).
concerns_for_reviewer: Csendes et al. Results paragraph 8 cites Supplementary Table 1 for the Pearson Delta DE and target-gene results, which are in Supplementary Table 2. Treated as a citation slip.
Supplementary Table 2 leaves the Wilcoxon-based Pearson Delta DE blank for scGPT and scFoundation on all four datasets (8 cells); the extractor asserts the blanks and records no result for them.
The extractor checks the printed Train Mean, scGPT, scFoundation and RF_go Pearson Delta values against Results paragraph 6 to three decimals; all 16 agree.

Origin: baselines (Train Mean, RF, EN, kNN) are author_reported, because the authors built them and argue that baselines win; scGPT and scFoundation are independent_paper, reproduced by the authors from the developers' code.
All four judgements are proxy, consistent with the three existing ones: expression-prediction scores do not establish mechanism or experimental prioritisation (use-case exclusion).
